new_statements.quote: Stress is lexically determined in Arguni and can fall on any syllable (see the examples in 15). Penultimate stress is the most common. (16) shows two stress minimal pairs. (15) Final stress: mardené [mar.de.ˈneː] ‘in three days’ / Penultimate stress: uririá”ir [u.ɾi.ˈɾja.ʔːirː] ‘ancestors’ / Antipenultimate stress: putíggyafwa [pu.ˈti.ɟːa.ɸwaː] ‘beach’ / Preantipenultimate stress: aérafai [a.ˈeː.ɾa.ɸa.ji] ‘cannot’ (16) ússu [ˈʔu.sːuː] ‘penis’ / ussú [ʔu.ˈsːuː] (trucated form of ussúfir ‘you go down’ …) gána [ˈgaː.naː] ‘I am’/‘I am from’ / ganá [ga.ˈnaː] ‘I put’. Some verb lexemes specify that stress must fall on the first-attaching prefix, e.g. -ssa ‘go up’.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (80 pp., born-digital xdvipdfmx/LaTeX PDF, text layer present, no scanned needed; title page: 'Linguistics RMA Final Thesis / A sketch grammar of Arguni / Pietro Milano / UU supervisor: Dr. Joost Zwarts, Second supervisor: Dr. Eline Visser'). Ran extracted text on pages 6-11, 16-17, 19-20 myself. §3.2 'Stress' is on PDF page 16 = printed p. 16 (page footers match PDF page numbers). The passage is there word for word: 'Stress is lexically determined in Arguni and can fall on any syllable (see the examples in 15). Penultimate stress is the most common. (16) shows two stress minimal pairs.' followed by example (15) with Final / Penultimate / Antipenultimate / Preantipenultimate stress (…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is a lexical property of each word (contrastive: minimal pairs ússu/ussú, gána/ganá) and may fall on the final, penultimate, antepenultimate or pre-antepenultimate syllable; the penult is the most frequent position. A class of verbs (e.g. -ssa 'go up', -agin 'give', ná 'put') lexically requires stress on the first prefix attached to the root (subject prefix, pluractional fa-, or a CV reduplicant). Stress is marked orthographically with an acute accent in the thesis.
new_statements.exceptions: Verbs whose lexical specification places stress on the first-attaching prefix rather than the root (fn. 15: such verbs must always carry a prefix); plural-possessor suffix -si moves the stress (p. ~35, §on possessive affixes); the only attested case of stress on a suffix noted in one lexeme; partial reduplication targets the stressed syllable and keeps penultimate stress in prefix-stressed verbs (§4.1); unstressed final syllables are subject to deletion/syncope (§3.4.4). Words without an acute in the wordlist are either prefix-stressed verbs or not yet transcribed for stress (Appendix A note).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level: the author states that Arguni lexemes consist of segments plus 'information about the position of the word stress' (§3, p. 11); examples are citation-form words and inflected verbs; possessive particles are described as usually unstressed in the phrase.
new_statements.identity_note: Milano 2025 describes the Arguni (Táfer) variety spoken in Arguni village on Arguni Island, i.e. argu1237 itself, which he treats as one member of the Arguni-Mbaruan-Yarikman (= Glottolog 'Nuta', bomb1263) dialect/language group alongside Mbaruan (Bedoanas, bedo1237 / ISO bed) and Yarikman (Erokwanas, ISO erw). Data from fieldwork Dec 2024 - Feb 2025 in Arguni village. Note Glottolog 5.3 classifies Arguni under Tanimbar-Bomberai > Nuta, not SHWNG as older sources did.
